summary: Feed s063_single is degraded: 6.9% packet loss (117/1697 TCP packets with gaps) exceeds 1% threshold. APM will see incomplete transactions. Other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, VLANs, encryption, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream capture is dropping packets before the APM - 6.9% TCP gaps indicate SPAN/mirror port oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion under burst. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is at the SPAN/broker ingress, not the 10G tool port itself.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires both directions and will see incomplete flows, missing segments and retransmissions. Results in inaccurate latency/response-time calculations, broken transaction correlation, and missed application performance degradations.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN ports drop packets when oversubscribed or congested; a passive TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy to the packet broker, eliminating the 6.9% ingress loss and restoring complete TCP streams for APM without needing payload slicing/filtering yet.
